season_awards.rederivation_notes: Own chain written before reading the record: AP award winner = highest total of ballot points over a 50-voter panel; need ballot length and point scale per award per season, placement counts, first-place votes, tie rule, ballot close date, plus candidate production, team success and position features. Independent searches (2026-11-09, search-result text only; cbssports.com did not resolve) returned: an AP statement quoted as 'top five picks for MVP and top three picks for other awards' from 2022 (Pro Football Network scale 10-5-3-2-1 MVP, 5-3-1 others, single source); 2024 OPOY tally Barkley 406/35 with Chase 0-25-8-10-2 (five places, 10-5-3-2-1); 2024 MVP Allen 378 (27-21-1-0-0). Differences from record: the record marks the 5-3-1 scheme as unsupported/unverified, but a quoted AP statement for 2022 exists in search text, so the non-MVP move to top-5 happened between 2022 and 2024 and is not dated; it still rests on unfetched copies.

findings.text: Every ballot fact (50 voters, top-5 10-5-3-2-1, 2023 and 2025 tallies, all eight awards top-5 in 2025) rests on WebSearch snippet text; no AP or publisher page was fetched (cbssports, wtop, apnews, si hosts blocked). Catalog text in nfl.vote_outcome_model says 'verified for 2023 and 2025'; 'verified' overstates search-copy evidence and should read 'seen in search-result copies'.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: 'verified' wording replaced by 'seen in search-result copies, primary page not fetched' across vote_outcome_model, split penalty, s6, variants; unverified source carried in u7b.

findings.text: evidence_zblk fact 1 labels the Stafford 366 / Maye 361 tally as the 2025 season but cites wtop.com/nfl/2025/02/ap-nfl-mvp-voting/, a Feb 2025 URL that would belong to the 2024 season (Allen 378). The season label and URL do not match; the search tool itself flagged the date ambiguity. Season attribution of the 366/361 tally is unconfirmed.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: evidence file and nfl.vote_outcome_model item (g) now state the 366/361 tally's season attribution is unconfirmed because the cited URL date is ambiguous.

findings.text: Evidence file says the earlier non-MVP 5-3-1 claim is 'NOT supported', but an independent search surfaced a quoted AP statement (2022: top five for MVP, top three for other awards) and 2024 OPOY with five places. The non-MVP scheme probably changed top-3 to top-5 between 2022 and 2024; catalog should say 'reported in search copies, unverified' rather than imply it was never used.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: 5-3-1 non-MVP scheme now described as reported in search copies of an AP statement, UNVERIFIED, change season unknown; evidence file no longer says 'unsupported'.

findings.text: 50-voter panel size is supported only for 2025 awards in the evidence file, yet the MVP definition states a 50-voter ballot generally; OPOY 272/14 is a paraphrase, not a quoted row. Tie rule and ballot close date stay unstated (flagged unverified).

unreg:team_window_event_hazards.reviewer: verifier-set1 NFL (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:team_window_event_hazards.rederivation_notes: Re-derivation from the contract text (Kalshi API: KXNFLNEXTINT has nine NYJ markets, 'before Week 2/4/.../16' and 'anytime in the 2026-27 season', all opened 2026-05-28, all finalized). Chain: games in window (1 game for Week 2 up to the full 17-game schedule) -> opposing starting QB per game -> opposing dropbacks (pass rate times plays, driven by script) -> per-dropback interception probability = league base times a defence factor (DB ball skills, pass rush, coverage scheme, defensive personnel changes) times a QB factor, with weather -> per-game count roughly Poisson with mean near 0.7-0.9 -> P(no INT) = product over games, fattened by a shared team-defence factor -> nested ladder across strikes, early finalization on the first interception. Note: I had already opened the record's catalog entry when I wrote this, so it is not blind; differences are in the findings. The record matches on the survival structure and shared factor, but misses the ladder and 17-game horizon, mis-specifies the hazard units, lacks a dropbacks input and lacks own-defence personnel.

findings.text: Hazard formula in nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_correlation and s3 is lambda = dropbacks x team defensive rate x opposing QB rate. Two per-attempt rates multiplied give rate squared, not a rate; it needs league-relative multipliers (lambda = dropbacks x p_league x d_team/p_league x q_QB/p_league or a log-additive model). nfl.opp_def_int_propensity is already QB-quality adjusted, so using nfl.int_rate beside it risks counting the QB twice. The core per-game expectation is not defined.

Contract structure missed. The API shows a nested ladder for one team: before Week 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 14, 16 and 'anytime' (W19), windows of 1 to about 17 games, all issued 2026-05-28 before Week 1, so the in-progress-at-issuance ambiguity the record centres on does not arise for listed markets, and N_g is not 'zero to about seven' (s1) nor history 'windows of 4-8 games'. The record says only one series and one window was sampled and never states monotone nesting across rungs or the long-horizon QB uncertainty a 17-game window brings. All nine sampled markets are finalized, so no live exposure.

The exposure term has no input: opposing dropbacks per game is attributed to nfl.pace, which measures neutral seconds per play (plays), and no pass-rate or dropback-volume input (nfl.script is not attached) converts plays into dropbacks. Dropbacks multiply the whole hazard, so the volume side of lambda is undefined.

Missing mechanism: the named team's own defensive personnel (cornerbacks and safeties with ball skills, their injuries, trades, scheme and coverage shell). role_personnel covers only opposing QBs and coaching_scheme is NOT_APPLICABLE on the claim pace and pass rush carry it; neither measures defensive-back availability or coverage scheme, which drives the defence factor over a 17-game window.

nfl.turnovers is the shared-factor control but is defined on giveaways, fumbles and fumble recoveries; a team-level interception takeaway rate is not isolated, so the shared defensive factor's width is estimated from a mixed turnover input.

Settlement source: record says the source is not named, but Kalshi series metadata lists settlement sources 'the Governing League' (nfl.com) and ESPN. Also undefined: interception on a two-point try, penalty-nullified interception (nflverse has a play_deleted flag), later stat corrections; only the first of these is mentioned.

Unsourced assertions: a backup quarterback 'usually throws interceptions at a higher rate', the threshold shape of the QB nonlinearity, and a per-game P(at least one) left as a placeholder. nflverse fields interception, qb_dropback, sack, qb_hit, passer_player_id, defteam, season_type exist in the data dictionary I fetched, but QB starter vintages and the interception-per-game base rate were not checked.
